newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe central bank ups statutory reserve ratio.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe central bank ups statutory reserve ratio.

text.p: Zimbabwe's central Reserve Bank on Friday raised to 20 percent from 17.5 percent its statutory reserve requirement ratio on all deposit liabilities of commercial and merchant banks.
The central bank said in a statement the new ratio was effective from December 6 and applied to domestic and foreign currency balances.

"With effect from 6 December 1996, the statutory reserve requirement ratio on all deposit liabilities of commercial banks and merchant banks will be raised to 20 percent from the current level of 17.5 percent," it said.

It said the measure was aimed at curbing a continuing buildup of excess liquidity in the money market which economists say is undermining efforts to bring down annual inflation -- pegged at 20.2 percent in October -- and keep interest rates low.
The bank also said compliance with the statutory reserve requirement would now be on a weekly basis beginning the week ending December 6.
No comment on the Reserve Bank announcement could be obtained from the market as the statement came after business had closed for the weekend.
